summary: Jeff Shore is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He served as a professor at Hanazono University from around 1991 to 2023, where he became professor emeritus around 2023.
Jeff Watt is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied under teacher Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.

Jeff Wilson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, mentored by Taitetsu Unno (attested 2009) and postdoctoral mentor Myosei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long specializes in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned a BA from the University of Notre Dame and an MA and PhD from the University of Chicago, later becoming Associate Professor of Religion and Asian Studies at Elizabethtown College in 2000.

Jeffrey Broughton works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1975 and held a post as professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University, Long Beach, attested in 2004.

Jeffrey Clark Ruff is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees from Missouri State University and a PhD from UC Santa Barbara under David Gordon White, later serving as an assistant professor at Marshall University in 2002.

Jeffrey Davis Schoening specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), studying under doctoral supervisor Collett Cox and advisor Sanghasen Singh.

Jeffrey Hopkins was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Geshe Wangyal, Ngawang Wangyal, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and the 14th Dalai Lama, earning a PhD from UW–Madison. He was a professor and center director at the University of Virginia (1973–2005).

Jeffrey J. Kripal specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1993) and became the J. Newton Rayzor Chair and Religion Department chair at Rice University in 2002.

Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned degrees from Komazawa University and Leiden University (PhD under James A. Benn) and held posts at McMaster University, the Max Planck Institute, and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman is a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He held positions at Cornell, Yale, and Johns Hopkins, before becoming University Professor and Professor of French Literature at Boston University around 1984, alongside several visiting professorships.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned his BA and PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and held posts including Professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (1981–1992) and positions at Toronto and Auckland.

Jeffrey Newmark is a scholar in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard University (~1992–1996) and the University of British Columbia (~2003–2009), and held a post at the University of Winnipeg.

Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara. He held posts at Berry College and the University of Virginia (attested 2003).

Jeffrey Samuels is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under W. S. Karunatillake and Karen Christina Lang, earning a PhD from the University of Virginia (attested 2002), and became Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).

Jeffrey Stout works in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at Brown University and earning his PhD from Princeton University (~1972–1976), he served as a professor at Princeton University from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from UNC Wilmington, UT Knoxville, and a PhD from UCLA under Gregory Schopen. He taught at UCLA and was a lecturer at UC San Diego (both attested 2013).

Jenkuan Shih is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Shih earned a master's degree supervised by Geshe Lhundup Sopa and completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under doctoral supervisors Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi.

Jennifer Jung-Kim is a scholar in history/archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Her career includes posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she is attested as assistant director (2016) and lecturer (2026).

Jenny Hung is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She earned PhDs from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and Lingnan University, and serves as an Assistant Professor in the Division of Humanities at HKUST.
